node.title: A=1 core-one zero-weld quartic boundary
node.statement: On the official A=1 core-one maximal-degree face, the two-sided weld can have K=0 only when b=0 and D_*=1. In that sole branch the full residual generator is irreducible and factors a separated difference F(U,V)-G_0(X)=Q_*V_0, where deg F=4e, deg G_0=8e+4, G_0 is supported on all but exactly three residual-domain points, deg Q_*=(2e+1,e), and deg V_0=(6e+3,3e). Thus Q_* is a one-quarter bidegree factor of a quartic separated boundary. Every other residual profile, D_*=0 profile, and exceptional-factor allocation has K nonzero. The quartic boundary and nonzero-K branch remain open.
